C-EXPLAIN-COVERAGE.Problem:
**Shared shape.** `getLintIssueGuide` already imports the review and gate surfaces, then ignores the guide objects those surfaces already hold, and there is no test whose universe is the codes this binary **constructs**. Three facts at authoring HEAD `0764686`:
| item | what it says | what it is bound to | | P1.1 | `--explain` teaches the fix | prefix / boilerplate text for review.* and gate.* | | P1.2 | every emittable code has a surface-specific guide | no finite constructed-code universe; `xml.*` / `design-context.*` / most `health.*` are prefix-open | | P1.3 | the default lint report points at `--explain` | `formatTextReport` prints severity, code, location, message only |
---

`classifyIssueCode` stays a separate fact: review and gate codes remain `emittable-uncatalogued` unless they become keys of `EXACT_GUIDES`, which they must not (F10 namespace: review findings are not lint exact entries).

Classification remains `emittable-uncatalogued`. None of those codes is a key of `EXACT_GUIDES`. **HEAD today:** `getLintIssueGuide("review.scope-outside-write-scope")` and `getLintIssueGuide("gate.apply.no-verdict")` return the dedicated-entry boilerplate; CLI `--explain review.scope-outside-write-scope` prints `Classification: emittable-uncatalogued` and matches `/ngrace review/i` because of that boilerplate, not because it read the catalog. **Failure conditions:** synthesized `toTitleFromCode` kept as the title while the explanation is swapped; only one code sampled; review/gate added to `EXACT_GUIDES`; classification changed to `exact`; assertion greps `guideFor` / `GATE_CATALOG` identifiers instead of comparing returned fields to the catalog object.

That coverage test asserts: for every universe code, the resolution path (`getLintIssueGuideResolution`) is exact, prefix, review-catalog, or gate-catalog — not emittable-fallback and not unknown. AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FIX-SHAPE:
Fixture-bound membership, closed by identity (not a count this change moves): `change.task-invalid-dependency`, `change.task-unknown-dependency`, `change.task-self-dependency`, `change.task-dependency-cycle`, `change.task-duplicate-dependency`, and `markup.unparsed-link-token`. All five `change.task-*dependency*` codes are required red-to-green members. `markup.unparsed-link-token` is the discrimination anchor, already green at HEAD, and is not a red. For each of those codes, `--explain` remediation and the **emitted issue message** from a fixture that actually fires the code agree on the accepted repair shapes that message names. Binding is shape-agreement, not a substring copy of the message into the test and not a word-hunt for tokens such as "canonical". Proven by the review-replay fixture (VerificationIntent): plant each fixture-bound failure, collect that code's own `issue.message`, run `--explain` / `getLintIssueGuide`, assert the guide's remediation names the same accepted shapes.
For `change.task-invalid-dependency` those shapes are the three `invalidMessage` already emits: multi-value text list of T-NNN ids (comma, semicolon, or whitespace); Task-element children holding a T-NNN id; self-closing T-NNN anchor children. A guide that is topical ("this is a dependency problem") but names none of those shapes, or that says the token must be canonical when the token already is, fails.
For the four siblings the token is already a valid T-NNN; the emitted messages name graph repairs, not authoring shapes: unknown target (`depends on unknown task`); self-edge (`cannot depend on itself`); duplicate listing (`repeats dependency`); cycle (`dependency cycle involving`). A guide that copies `invalidMessage`'s three DependsOn shapes onto those codes, or that is merely topical, fails — the token already is canonical.
**HEAD today (measured on the shipped binary):** `change.task-invalid-dependency` — family title "neo-grace Change Lifecycle Issue"; remediation is keep-drafts-active / move-applied to archive; does not name the three DependsOn shapes; emitted message does. The four siblings share that same HEAD `--explain` body; each emitted message names its graph failure, not archive placement. `markup.unparsed-link-token` — exact guide already names accepted families and `[,;\\s]+`; agrees with `unparsedLinkTokenMessage`; **green at HEAD** (not a red).
Residual (disclosure, not a NonGoal): `review.scope-outside-write-scope`, `gate.apply.no-verdict`, and `health.required-log-marker-not-found` remain in `AC-COVERAGE-NO-BOILERPLATE`'s constructed-code delta and still get real guides. This bundle asserts the P1.1 wire, not the quality of the review and gate catalogs' own remediation text. Health is not emitted through lint, so a lint fixture cannot plant it; after the wire the review and gate codes are satisfied by catalog-object field equality (`AC-WIRE-CATALOG-GUIDES`) and are not independent fix-shape evidence.
**Failure conditions:** family lifecycle remediation left in place; "must be canonical" as the only repair; three-shape DependsOn text copied onto a sibling whose token is already valid T-NNN; test greps `issue.message` into the guide or greps isolated words from the message; only `markup.unparsed-link-token` asserted (already green); only `change.task-invalid-dependency` asserted (four siblings left on the family guide); set replaced by a count; fixture omitted so the bind is a catalog-to-catalog comparison.
